# Building the custom RDKit MinimalLib WASM (Spin 3D fast embed)

The stock `@rdkit/rdkit` MinimalLib exposes **2D coordinates only** — no 3D
embedding. This is a *patched* MinimalLib that adds two `JSMol` methods —
`generate_3d_embed` and `optimize_3d_conformer` — and links RDKit's conformer +
force-field libraries into the JS (Embind) target. ETKDGv3 embedding is the Spin 3D
fast-embed engine (replacing OpenChemLib's ~45 s embed; see
`docs/benchmarks/spin3d-rdkit-native-spike.md` — native RDKit does it in ~1 s).

**The compile is deferred** (needs Docker + Emscripten, multi-GB, long). Everything
needed to reproduce it is pinned here.

## Pin
- RDKit tag: **`Release_2026_03_3`**
- Commit: **`e74e7b0a5a2fc4e7f77c04ec26a61d4b8edbf22f`**
- Matches the native-spike RDKit version (algorithm parity with the recorded benchmark).
- License: **BSD-3-Clause** — bundle RDKit's `license.txt` next to the artifacts.

## Patches (`./patches/`, apply with `patch -p1` from the rdkit repo root)
| Patch | Effect |
|---|---|
| `0001-…CMakeLists.txt.patch` | Adds `DistGeomHelpers;ForceFieldHelpers;DistGeometry;ForceField;Alignment` to `MINIMAL_LIB_LIBRARIES` (the `RDKit_minimal` Embind target — these were CFFI-only before). |
| `0002-…minilib.h.patch` | Declares `generate_3d_embed` / `optimize_3d_conformer` on `JSMolBase`. |
| `0003-…minilib.cpp.patch` | Implements them: `addHs` → `EmbedMolecule(ETKDGv3, {seed,maxIterations,timeout,enforceChirality,useRandomCoords})`; `MMFF/UFFOptimizeMolecule`. Returns the JSON payload below. |
| `0004-…jswrapper.cpp.patch` | Registers both methods in `class_<JSMolBase>("Mol")`. |
| `0006-minimallib-tpsa-includeSandP.patch` | Adds an optional details-JSON argument to `get_descriptors` and honours `{"includeSandP":true}` by recomputing **only** `tpsa` through RDKit's own `calcTPSA(m, force, includeSandP)`. Every other descriptor stays exactly as `Descriptors::Properties` produced it. Without it the Properties calculator hard-codes `includeSandP=false`, so every sulfonamide and phosphate reads low with no way to ask for the other convention (PLANS.md §7). Touches `common.h`, `minilib.h`, `minilib.cpp`, `jswrapper.cpp`; the embind registration follows the existing `get_morgan_fp` `select_overload` idiom. |
| `0005-build-freetype-mirror-…patch` | Build-env fix: points the deps Dockerfile's FreeType download at a SourceForge mirror (the pinned savannah.gnu.org URL was returning 502). FreeType is only used for MolDraw2D SVG fonts, unrelated to 3D embedding — only needed because the deps image builds it unconditionally. |

`0001–0004` were generated by diffing the pinned source files and verified to apply
cleanly (`patch -p1 --dry-run`); `0005` patches the build's deps Dockerfile. `0006` was
generated the same way and verified to apply **in sequence after `0001–0005`** against a
pristine checkout of the pinned commit.

## Patch budget
**Six patches.** PLANS.md §7 tracks this deliberately: every patch is a rebuild obligation, and
a tenth is a maintenance smell. Record the count in
`docs/architecture/dependency-inventory.md` whenever it changes.

> ⚠️ **Two changes are pending a rebuild.** The committed `RDKit_minimal.{js,wasm}` below were
> built from patches `0001–0005` as they stood in June 2026, so they carry **neither** of these:
>
> 1. **`useRandomCoords`** (patch `0003`) — see the note below.
> 2. **`includeSandP`** (patch `0006`) — `get_descriptors` in the committed artifact takes no
>    arguments. Measured against the real binary, passing one does **not** throw: it is silently
>    ignored, and `CS(=O)(=O)C` returns `tpsa` 34.14 either way. `detectEngineCapabilities` in
>    `src/analysis.ts` therefore probes by **value**, not by whether the call succeeded — arity
>    detection would report the patch as present and label an S-excluded number with the S-included
>    convention. Until a rebuild lands, `rdkit.tpsa` stays at version 1.0.0 and its contract says the
>    convention is not selectable.
>
> ⚠️ **Rebuild detail for `useRandomCoords`.** The committed `RDKit_minimal.{js,wasm}`
> below were built **before** `0003` gained the `useRandomCoords` parameter, so they
> ignore it. ETKDG's default (eigenvalue-decomposition) start *fails* to embed large,
> flexible molecules — e.g. a ~234-heavy-atom peptide returns no conformer (verified: native
> RDKit 2026.03.3 `EmbedMolecule` returns -1 with `useRandomCoords=False`, succeeds with
> `True`). `packages/rdkit-adapter/src/conformer.ts` already retries such embeds with
> `useRandomCoords:true`, but that only takes effect once these artifacts are **rebuilt** from
> the patched tree (and the SHA-256s below refreshed). Until then the conformer worker falls
> back to the OpenChemLib engine for structures RDKit can't embed.

## Build
```bash
# 1. Clone the pinned source and apply our patches.
git clone https://github.com/rdkit/rdkit.git rdkit-src
cd rdkit-src
git checkout e74e7b0a5a2fc4e7f77c04ec26a61d4b8edbf22f
for p in /path/to/packages/rdkit-adapter/vendor/patches/*.patch; do patch -p1 < "$p"; done

# 2. Build MinimalLib from the local (patched) tree via the RDKit Docker flow.
cd Code/MinimalLib/docker
GET_SRC=copy_from_local docker compose -f docker_compose_build_minimallib.yml build \
  --build-arg "EXCEPTION_HANDLING=-fwasm-exceptions" 2>&1 | tee docker-compose.log

# 3. Export the artifacts (lands in Code/MinimalLib/demo/).
DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build -f Dockerfile_4_rdkit_export -o ../demo .
```

cp Code/MinimalLib/demo/RDKit_minimal.js   packages/rdkit-adapter/vendor/RDKit_minimal.js
cp Code/MinimalLib/demo/RDKit_minimal.wasm packages/rdkit-adapter/vendor/RDKit_minimal.wasm
cp rdkit-src/license.txt                   packages/rdkit-adapter/vendor/RDKit-LICENSE.txt
# Record hashes in this file (replace the TODOs):
shasum -a 256 packages/rdkit-adapter/vendor/RDKit_minimal.{js,wasm}

## Smoke test (gate before integrating)
With Node, load the artifact and embed the exact offending molfile and confirm it
matches the native spike (≤ a few seconds, all stereo preserved):
```js
const initRDKitModule = require("./RDKit_minimal.js");
const fs = require("node:fs");
initRDKitModule().then((RDKit) => {
  const molblock = fs.readFileSync("docs/benchmarks/offending-chemdraft.mol", "utf8");
  const mol = RDKit.get_mol(molblock);
  const t = Date.now();
  const embed = JSON.parse(mol.generate_3d_embed(JSON.stringify({ seed: 42, timeoutSeconds: 10 })));
  console.log("embedOk", embed.embedOk, "ms", Date.now() - t,
              "engineAtoms", embed.coords3dByEngineAtom.length / 3,
              "addedH", embed.generatedHydrogenEngineAtoms.length);
  // refine re-derives a pristine copy from the embed molblock (no long-lived handle):
  const work = RDKit.get_mol(embed.molblock, JSON.stringify({ removeHs: false }));
  const refined = JSON.parse(work.optimize_3d_conformer(JSON.stringify({ forceField: "mmff94", maxIters: 200 })));
  console.log("ff", refined.forceField);
  work.delete();
  mol.delete();
});
```
Then run the *worker-realistic* benchmark (the real gate): load the `.wasm` the way the
app will (Vite `?url` import in `conformerWorker.ts`) and measure WASM init / first /
warmed embed — target warmed embed ≤ 2–3 s (hard cap 5 s).

## JSON payload contract (consumed by `packages/rdkit-adapter/src/conformer.ts`)
`generate_3d_embed(detailsJson)` and `optimize_3d_conformer(detailsJson)` return:
```jsonc
{
  "embedOk": true,                       // false => embed/timeout/FF-setup failed; fall back per policy
  "coords3dByEngineAtom": [x0,y0,z0,…],  // ENGINE-atom order, length nEngine*3, y-up frame
  "engineToOriginalAtom": [0,1,2,-1,…],  // -1 = RDKit-added H/extra (read from the per-atom prop)
  "generatedHydrogenEngineAtoms": [64,…],
  "molblock": "…3D engine-order molblock…",  // generate_3d_embed ONLY — pristine copy for refine
  "forceField": { "name":"MMFF94", "status":"converged|not-converged|setup-failed",
                  "energy": -12.3, "iterations": 200 } // optimize_3d_conformer ONLY
}
```
- `details` for embed: `{ seed, maxIterations, timeoutSeconds }`.
- `details` for optimize: `{ forceField: "mmff94"|"mmff94s"|"uff", maxIters }`.
- The adapter scatters `coords3dByEngineAtom` onto original atoms via
  `engineToOriginalAtom` (stored from the embed). On the refine copy the atom props are
  absent, so its `engineToOriginalAtom` is all `-1` and is ignored — the adapter reuses
  the embed's mapping (engine atom order is identical because the refine re-parses the
  embed molblock).
- The payload is **plain data** (structured-clone-safe). No `JSMol` handle is kept on the
  JS side between calls — each `get_mol` is `.delete()`d within the call, so there is no
  WASM-heap lifecycle to leak.
